result.topic_en: Page 120 contains the end of an unsolved question by Moutard on quadric surfaces through a curve and anallagmatic quartics, followed by question 729 (1865) by J.-J.-A. Mathieu on the directions of the axes of a plane section of a quadric.
result.transcription:
( 120 )
deuxième courbe située, comme la première, sur une infinité de surfaces du second ordre.
Cela posé, on demande de démontrer que les axes de chacune de ces nouvelles surfaces sont parallèles aux normales qu'on peut mener en O aux trois *anallagmatiques* du quatrième ordre, passant par ce point, qui ont pour *focale* la courbe donnée.
MOUTARD.

729 (1865, 142). — Les directions des axes de la section faite par le plan
$x\cos\alpha + y\cos\beta + z\cos\gamma = \lambda,$
dans la surface
$Ax^2 + A'y^2 + A''z^2 + 2Byz + 2B'zx + 2B''xy + 2Cx + 2C'y + 2C''z + D = 0,$
sont données par les intersections du plan
$x\cos\alpha + y\cos\beta + z\cos\gamma = 0$
avec le cône
$(A\cos^2\beta + A'\cos^2\alpha - 2B''\cos\alpha\cos\beta)(x^2\sin^2\beta - y^2\sin^2\alpha)$
$+ (A\cos^2\gamma + A''\cos^2\alpha - 2B'\cos\alpha\cos\gamma)(z^2\sin^2\alpha - x^2\sin^2\gamma)$
$+ (A'\cos^2\gamma + A''\cos^2\beta - 2B\cos\beta\cos\gamma)(y^2\sin^2\gamma - z^2\sin^2\beta) = 0.$
J.-J.-A. MATHIEU.

second curve lying, like the first, on infinitely many surfaces of the second order.
This being established, it is required to prove that the axes of each of these new surfaces are parallel to the normals that can be drawn at O to the three fourth-order *anallagmatic* surfaces passing through this point which have the given curve as *focal* curve.

questions.statement_en:
The directions of the axes of the section made by the plane
$x\cos\alpha + y\cos\beta + z\cos\gamma = \lambda,$
in the surface
$Ax^2 + A'y^2 + A''z^2 + 2Byz + 2B'zx + 2B''xy + 2Cx + 2C'y + 2C''z + D = 0,$
are given by the intersections of the plane
$x\cos\alpha + y\cos\beta + z\cos\gamma = 0$
with the cone
$(A\cos^2\beta + A'\cos^2\alpha - 2B''\cos\alpha\cos\beta)(x^2\sin^2\beta - y^2\sin^2\alpha)$
$+ (A\cos^2\gamma + A''\cos^2\alpha - 2B'\cos\alpha\cos\gamma)(z^2\sin^2\alpha - x^2\sin^2\gamma)$
$+ (A'\cos^2\gamma + A''\cos^2\beta - 2B\cos\beta\cos\gamma)(y^2\sin^2\gamma - z^2\sin^2\beta) = 0.$
